definitions.explanation: A person's surname before marriage or a legal name change. In Japan, married couples must share one surname by law, so one partner's pre-marriage name becomes their former surname.

examples.japanese: {旧姓|きゅうせい}は{田中|たなか}です。
{職場|しょくば}では{旧姓|きゅうせい}を{使|つか}い{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: I continue to use my maiden name at work.

examples.japanese: {旧姓|きゅうせい}の{使用|しよう}を{認|みと}める{企業|きぎょう}が{増|ふ}えてきたが、{法的|ほうてき}には{認|みと}められていない。
examples.english: More companies are allowing the use of maiden names, but it is not legally recognized.

notes:
USAGE:
Under Japanese law ({民法|みんぽう}), married couples must adopt the same surname. In practice, the wife usually takes the husband's name, making her pre-marriage name her {旧姓|きゅうせい}. The topic of {選択的|せんたくてき}{夫婦|ふうふ}{別姓|べっせい} (optional separate surnames for married couples) is an ongoing social debate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧姓|きゅうせい}を{使|つか}う: to use one's maiden name
- {旧姓|きゅうせい}に{戻|もど}す: to revert to one's maiden name
- {旧姓|きゅうせい}{使用|しよう}: use of maiden name

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {姓|せい}: surname, family name
- {名字|みょうじ}: surname (everyday term)
- {本名|ほんみょう}: real name
